description: The 'other China' in Congo: hundreds of small Chinese gold operators in the east - a dimension absent from the original source documents
verification_status: confirmed by multiple sources (Reuters/AFP via ADF, VOA, AP, IFRI, Business & Human Rights Centre)
key_thesis: The original materials describe China in the DRC only as organized state corporations in Katanga - orderly, large, under contract. But a fundamentally different Chinese layer exists in the east: hundreds of small and mid-sized companies mining gold outside the law. This is not one strategy but two unrelated ones - and the second is steadily undermining the legitimacy of the first.

scale.companies_in_south_kivu: per the governor, over 147 Chinese companies operating illegally; in June 2024, 547 companies were identified as operating illegally; separate publications cite an estimate of 'over 450 illegal mines, mostly under Chinese management'
scale.output: according to South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, such companies each mine at least 100 kg of gold per month
scale.workaround_scheme: DRC's mining code bars foreigners from artisanal mining; Chinese companies form 'partnerships' with local cooperatives and operate through them, without declaring profits or paying taxes
scale.technical_edge: mechanized excavators and dredges versus local artisanal miners' picks and shovels

conflict_timeline.event: the South Kivu governor suspends 9 Chinese companies in Mwenga; China's MFA (Wu Peng) publicly orders companies from Zhejiang and Jiangsu to shut down and leave the province
Governor Purusi suspends ALL mining activity in the province, giving 72 hours to vacate sites; instead of the 117 illegal companies invited to formalize, 540 showed up
17 Chinese nationals arrested at a mine in Karhembo; 14 were released and returned to China despite $10m in unpaid taxes and fines
three Chinese nationals arrested with 10 gold bars and $400,000 in cash
PRECEDENT: a Bukavu court sentences three men to 7 years in prison and a $600,000 fine - the DRC's first-ever conviction of foreign mineral brokers
mass protests in Bukavu after an earlier-detained group of Chinese nationals was released
the DRC Ministry of Justice declares Masisi (North Kivu) and Kalehe (South Kivu) 'red zones' with a 6-month mining and trading ban
a Chinese company reports M23 forces looted ~$70m in gold in South Kivu, declares force majeure, prepares lawsuits
a new three-month mining suspension in Mwenga and Shabunda
DRC and China sign a police-cooperation agreement against mining fraud and cybercrime

collateral_damage.smuggling: per Finance Minister Nicolas Kazadi (2023), the DRC loses roughly $1bn a year to minerals smuggled into Rwanda alone
collateral_damage.environment: one South Kivu site that began operating in 2019 near Kitumba had lost about 82 hectares of forest cover by June 2023 (Berggorilla & Regenwald)
collateral_damage.militarization: IFRI documents militarization of mining sites and violence against civilians, including complicity by soldiers
collateral_damage.chinese_casualties: a militia attack on a gold mine in Ituri (2024) killed six Chinese miners and two Congolese soldiers

why_it_matters: This layer, not Sicomines, is what shapes how ordinary Congolese in the east perceive China. Beijing is publicly distancing itself - its own foreign ministry ordered companies to leave, and in 2026 it moved to police cooperation with Kinshasa. In effect, the Chinese state is paying a reputational price for actors it does not control.
